key_insight: LGTM (Less Gaussians, Texture More) replaces dense pixel-aligned Gaussian prediction with a compact set of Gaussian primitives augmented by per-primitive textures, breaking the quadratic primitive growth with resolution and enabling feed‑forward 4K synthesis.
problem_solved: Existing feed-forward Gaussian splatting methods scale poorly: predicting pixel-aligned primitives causes primitive count to grow quadratically with image resolution, making high‑resolution (e.g., 4K) synthesis infeasible.
method: Predict a compact set of geometric Gaussian primitives instead of dense pixel-aligned Gaussians to reduce primitive count.
Attach high‑resolution, per‑primitive textures that decouple appearance detail from geometric complexity.
Render using textured splatting in a feed‑forward pipeline to synthesize high‑resolution images efficiently (4K capable).
impact: Enables memory- and compute-efficient high‑resolution neural rendering pipelines, making practical 4K feed‑forward synthesis for applications like content creation, AR/VR, and real‑time graphics.
visual_elements: Line chart: primitive count vs image resolution comparing quadratic growth (pixel‑aligned) to the compact LGTM curve
Pipeline diagram: input → compact Gaussians + per‑primitive textures → textured splatting → 4K output
Before/after render comparison: baseline dense splatting vs LGTM output at 4K (same scene)
Bar chart: memory and inference time comparison (baseline vs LGTM) at multiple resolutions
paper_title: Less Gaussians, Texture More: 4K Feed-Forward Textured Splatting
paper_authors: Yixing Lao, Xuyang Bai, Xiaoyang Wu, Nuoyuan Yan, Zixin Luo
